opening_message:
Ticket 1: Erika Bolton (employee ID E002) requests admin access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E002.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: E002 (Erika Bolton) is a full-time Analyst requesting admin access to Payroll. As a full-time employee, admin requires the employee's role to own the system; Payroll is owned by Payroll Specialist, not Analyst, so access is capped at write. Recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: E002 (Erika Bolton) is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors can have read, or write only with advanced training; never admin. Requested admin for Payroll exceeds max, so cap at read. Recommend granting read.
reason: E002 (Erika Bolton) requested admin access to Payroll. The HR note identifies E002 as a full-time Analyst. Payroll is owned by the Payroll Specialist role, not Analyst, so per policy admin is not permitted for this full-time employee; the maximum allowed is write. Since the requested level (admin) exceeds the maximum (write), the maximum is granted. (Note: the security note lists the employee as a contractor with basic training, which would cap at read; however, based on the HR employment record indicating full-time Analyst, access is granted at write, which is within the full-time cap and below the requested admin.)
